title: Corey Haines' playbook for competitor and alternative pages that rank and convert
summary: A practical playbook for building four formats of competitor pages (alternative, alternatives, you-vs-them, A-vs-B) that capture comparison search intent. It stresses honest, evidence-backed claims, centralized competitor data, and a recurring audit to keep public claims accurate.

principles.text: Be honest in comparison pages: acknowledge competitor strengths and your own limits, because readers will verify claims.
principles.quote: Acknowledge competitor strengths. Be accurate about your limitations. Don't misrepresent competitor features. Readers are comparing—they'll verify claims

principles.text: Go deeper than feature checklists: explain why differences matter with use cases and scenarios.
principles.quote: Go beyond feature checklists. Explain *why* differences matter. Include use cases and scenarios. Show, don't just tell

principles.text: Help evaluators decide by saying who you're best for and who the competitor is best for.
principles.quote: Different tools fit different needs. Be clear about who you're best for. Be clear about who competitor is best for. Reduce evaluation friction

principles.text: Match page format to search intent: switchers, researchers, direct comparers, and people comparing two rivals each get a different page.
principles.quote: Search intent: User is actively looking to switch from a specific competitor

principles.text: Treat 'not observed' as different from 'doesn't have'. Only mark a feature absent when docs or hands-on use confirm it, and date every competitor fact.
principles.quote: "Not observed" is not "doesn't have." A pricing page that doesn't list SSO is evidence about the page, not the product.

principles.text: Keep competitor data in one centralized source of truth so updates propagate across all pages, and re-verify on a schedule.
principles.quote: Competitor data should be centralized. Updates propagate to all pages. Single source of truth per competitor
